title: Rollback credit stickiness during route deprecation causes transient unmetered windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: When a route is deprecated/renamed and requests are routed via aliasing + rollback, org-level debit adjustments are reconciled but per-route debit state can become sticky. This leaves a short window where requests are effectively unmetered for the deprecated route or are double-counted against org budget after rollback. Observed in a canary during route rename traffic migration.

Why it matters: Customer-facing observed behavior includes: temporary burst of free requests for a small subset of keys, incorrect org-level usage spikes after rollback, and confusion for users relying on per-route quotas. This can cause billing disagreements and SLA anomalies for Dedicated customers with strict quotas.
reproduction_steps: Set up org-level quota + a per-route soft limit for route-A and route-B (route-B will be the new alias).
Start steady traffic to route-A and confirm meter increments on both route and org aggregates.
Rename route-A to route-B in control plane (route alias) and initiate a canary migration where some edge nodes route to new alias while others remain on old mapping.
Trigger a rollback (reverting alias mapping) before background reconciliation completes.

Observe metrics: route-level counters for route-A remain stale (showing reduced increments) while org-level counters reflect debits that were applied twice or not normalized depending on shard ordering.
investigation_notes: Initial logs show asymmetric ordering between debit-write-to-org-aggregator and per-route-checkpoint flush on shard replay.
Edge shards use local route mapping cache; stale mapping allowed a short grace period where debit tokens were applied against the alias mapping but route checkpoint persisted to old key namespace.
Race window appears when (1) alias change is propagated to some edge shards, (2) rolling rollback occurs, and (3) background reconciliation compaction runs concurrently.
Reproducer run captured a 600ms median divergence window where meter writes succeeded to org ledger while route ledger writes either were duplicated or lost depending on shard replay ordering.
No evidence of persistent data corruption; issue occurs on timing and ordering only and is mitigated by eventual reconciliation but not before customer-visible anomalies.
proposed_solution: Short term: Add a conservative lock-step reconciliation step when route alias state changes are rolled back within a short TTL. This means delaying final org ledger commits until per-route checkpoint delta confirms no conflicting replay in progress.

Mid term: Introduce idempotent route debit tokens with a namespace version embedded. When a mapping change occurs, debits include mapping-version so replays and rollbacks can be deduplicated deterministically.
Long term: Refactor shard-born reconciliation to perform two-phase commit for changes that affect both org and route ledgers when mapping updates are non-monotonic (rename/rollback).
Implement feature flag for conservative reconciliation to toggle on for Dedicated customers and ramp after smoke testing.
rollout_plan: Feature flag rollout to staging, run synthetic traffic reproducer for 48 hours.
Enable conservative reconciliation for a small set of Dedicated orgs in Canary region, monitor org vs route divergence metrics and billing deltas.
If canary stable for 72 hours, expand to 50% of Dedicated, then 100% over a week.
If regressions found, quickly toggle feature off (designed for quick rollback).
test_plan: Unit tests for mapping-versioned debit token creation and deduplication logic.
Integration test that simulates alias flip + rollback across N edge shards and asserts eventual consistency and no duplicate org debits.
Load test at 10k RPS with frequent alias flips to validate latencies and that the conservative path does not violate latency SLOs for high-tier customers.
Add new histogram metric for 'reconciliation-delay-ms' and alert if > 2000ms spikes during mapping changes.
metrics_and_dashboards: alert: route-org-delta-high (trigger if > 5% of org usage in 5m attributable to deprecated routes)
SLO check: reconciliation-latency.p50 < 300ms (target for conservative path)
postmortem KPI: count of rollback events that caused >1% transient free-window across orgs.
next_actions: Assign PR for mapping-versioned tokens: ENG-assign-001 (Marco).
Prototype two-phase commit gating in a staging cluster (Aisha + Marco).
Notify solutions engineering and support teams about temporary workaround: avoid rolling back alias mappings during migrations until we have conservative flag enabled.
Schedule follow-up review with Product and Reliability to discuss enabling for Dedicated customers.
